💡 Key Takeaways
  • QR codes are everywhere when we travel now, on restaurant tables, parking meters, hotel signs, airports, train stations, and transit machines.
  • QR code travel scam happens when a fake QR code sends travellers to a fraudulent website.
  • It has been revealed that A scammer does not always need to hack a system or damage a payment machine.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

QR codes are everywhere when we travel now, on restaurant tables, parking meters, hotel signs, airports, train stations, and transit machines. This travel scam known as Quishing or QR code phishing is becoming the fastest growing travel scam warning out there. Most QR codes are legitimate, but scammers are using fake QR code stickers and fake payment pages to catch travellers when they are tired, rushed, or distracted.

QR code travel scam happens when a fake QR code sends travellers to a fraudulent website. The code may be placed over a real QR code on a parking meter, restaurant table, hotel notice, airport sign, or transit machine, or it may arrive by text or email pretending to be a fine, toll, ticket, or check-in request. The safest rule is simple: Pause. Check. Then pay.Read out post: 20 Common Travel Scams and How to Avoid Them.

It has been revealed that A scammer does not always need to hack a system or damage a payment machine. Sometimes they print a fake QR code sticker and place it directly over a legitimate code.

From a quick glance, the sign still looks official. The logo may look familiar. The instructions may seem normal. The page that opens may copy the colours, layout, and branding of the real firm.

According to recent reports, you think you are paying for parking, ordering food, checking into a hotel, or settling a toll. Instead, criminals may be collecting your credit card number, password, phone number, licence plate, email address, or other personal information.

The FTC has also warned about fake traffic violation texts that begin with a QR code and try to scare people into paying a fake unpaid balance.

The FTC has warned that scammers hide harmful links in QR codes to steal personal information, including by placing fake QR codes over real ones on parking meters.

Recent findings suggest that many restaurants now use QR codes for menus, ordering, or payment. Most are legitimate, but travellers should still be cautious. This is the easiest travel scam for QR code phishing as everyone uses it.

A menu QR code should usually show a menu. Be careful if it asks for information it does not need, such as your passport number, banking details, hotel room number, or a password.

According to recent reports, before scanning a QR code on a restaurant table, look at the surface. Does it look printed into the menu or table sign, or does it look like a sticker placed on top? If it looks raised, crooked, bubbled, or mismatched, ask staff for a printed menu or the restaurant’s official website.

Parking is one of the easiest places for this scam to work because travellers are often rushed and confused.

In a recent development, you may not know the local parking app. You may be dealing with another language. You may be worried about getting a ticket. That pressure makes a “scan to pay” sticker feel helpful.

Before paying through a parking QR code, inspect the sticker, read the URL preview, and check whether the payment page matches the city, parking authority, or official app named on the machine.

If anything feels off, do not use the QR code. Type the official website yourself, use the official parking app, pay at the machine, or ask local staff for help.

Airports and transit stations are full of QR codes: Wi-Fi, directions, tickets, luggage storage, forms, lounge access, and service information. Travel scams often happen when travelers are in a hurry. If you need wifi, a taxi, some food, QR codes are often the easiest way to catch you off guard.

That does not mean every code is unsafe. It means you should slow down when a public QR code asks for payment, passwords, ID documents, or personal information.

The FBI warns that malicious QR codes can send people to fake sites, steal victim data, embed malware, or redirect payments. The FBI warns that criminals can tamper with QR codes to redirect payments, steal login and financial information, or send people to malicious websites.

The easiest way to avoid this scam is to build one habit before you scan a public QR code.

Do not scan just because a sign looks official. Public signs, parking meters, table cards, and posters can be tampered with.

If the message claims you must pay immediately, avoid a fine, settle a toll, confirm a booking, or prevent a penalty, slow down. Urgency is one of the biggest warning signs.

Before your phone opens anything, look at the QR code itself.

We call this the scratch test. You are not damaging the sign. You are simply checking whether the QR code feels or looks different from the rest of the surface.

Canadian readers can also check the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security’s QR code safety guidance and report fraud through the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.

In a recent development, most phones show a preview of the website before opening the page. Read it.

Look for misspellings, extra words, strange endings, random letters, shortened links, or a domain that does not match the company, hotel, restaurant, city, or attraction.

Do not rely only on the padlock symbol. A secure connection does not automatically mean the site is legitimate. The real question is whether you are on the correct website.

The FTC has also warned about fake traffic violation texts that include a QR code and pressure people to pay a fake unpaid balance.

For payments, passwords, account logins, or identity information, the safest option is often to bypass the QR code.

Open your browser and type the official website yourself. Use an app you already installed from the official app store. Ask an employee for the correct payment method. Contact your hotel, airline, rental car organization, or bank through the phone number on your booking or card — not through the number on a suspicious page.

First, do not panic. Scanning a QR code does not automatically mean your information has been stolen. The bigger risk usually begins when you enter payment information, type a password, download a file, or provide personal details.

If you scanned a suspicious code:.

Close the page immediately if the link looks wrong, the message creates urgency, or the site asks for information you did not expect to provide.

Do not download an unfamiliar app or file from a QR code.

If you entered credit card information, contact your bank or card issuer using the official number on the back of your card or through the official banking app.

In a recent development, if you entered a password, change it through the official website or app. If you reused that password anywhere else, change it there too.

It has been revealed that watch for follow-up messages. A scammer who has some of your information may later pretend to be your bank, hotel, airline, rental car tech giant, or payment provider.

Report the fake QR code to the business, parking authority, hotel, airport, or local authority so they can remove it.

A QR code may be suspicious if it looks like a sticker placed over another code, has peeling edges, opens a strange URL, uses a shortened link, creates urgency, asks for information that does not make sense, or directs you away from the official website or app.

Recent findings suggest that at a restaurant, a QR menu should not need your passport or banking password. At a parking meter, the payment page should match the city or parking authority. At a hotel, a check-in code should not send you to a random payment page outside the official booking system.

The BBB has also warned consumers to double-check QR codes before paying for parking.

No. QR codes are part of modern travel, and many are perfectly safe.

In a recent development, the goal is not to panic every time you see one. The goal is to stop treating every QR code as automatically trustworthy.

A few seconds of inspection can protect you from a much longer financial or account-recovery problem later.

QR codes are convenient, but convenience is exactly what scammers are using against travellers.

Before scanning a public QR code at a restaurant, parking meter, hotel, airport, train station, attraction, or transit stop, remember the rule:.

Inspect the code. Read the link. Go directly to the official website or app when money, passwords, or personal information are involved.

That tiny pause may be the thing that saves your trip.

It has been revealed that scanning a QR code is not automatically dangerous. The danger usually begins when you open a suspicious page, enter payment details, type a password, download a file, or provide personal information without checking whether the site is legitimate.

Inspect the physical code for stickers, raised edges, bubbles, peeling corners, or anything placed over another code. Then check the URL preview before opening the page. If the link looks strange or does not match the official manufacturer, city, hotel, or attraction, do not use it.

Recent findings suggest that before entering payment information, make sure the website belongs to the official business or authority. When in doubt, use the official app, type the website manually, pay directly at the machine, or ask staff for the correct payment method.

Recent findings suggest that contact your bank or card issuer immediately using the official number on the back of your card or your banking app. Watch for suspicious charges, replace the card if needed, and do not use any contact information from the suspicious website.

Sources indicate that growing up in Fort Lauderdale, the Bahamas always felt like an extension of South Florida to me. Each island has its own personality, and even after years of visiting, there are so many I still want to discover.

According to recent reports, renting a home is one of my favorite ways to experience it all. Beautiful beachfront villas, colorful cottages, and contemporary homes with pools overlooking the sea are everywhere in the Bahamas. 📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that senate Democratic leader Charles E.
  • Recent findings suggest that ANALYSIS -- “Life moves pretty fast,” that famed 20th-century philosopher Ferris Bueller once mentioned.
  • In 2024, Democrats were consigned to the political wilderness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer poses in his office on Nov. 9 for a group photo with incoming members of his caucus: from left, Ohio's Sherrod Brown, Texas' James Talarico, Iowa's Josh Turek, Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed, North Carolina's Roy Cooper, Illinois' Juliana Stratton, Fresh Hampshire's Chris Pappas, South Carolina's Annie Andrews, Minnesota's Peggy Flanagan, Maine's Troy Jackson and Kansas' Adam Hamilton. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

Recent findings suggest that ANALYSIS -- “Life moves pretty fast,” that famed 20th-century philosopher Ferris Bueller once mentioned. “If you don't stop and look around once in a while, you could miss it.”.

In 2024, Democrats were consigned to the political wilderness. Republicans had captured the White House, flipped the Senate and held the House. President Donald Trump had completely altered the party coalitions as he led the ascendant GOP to victory.

Now, just two years later, Democrats are on the rise. A historic midterm tsunami has swept them into such commanding Senate and House majorities that some are questioning whether Republicans will ever be in charge again. And if Texas is blue, how does the GOP have any chance in the Electoral College again?

A big takeaway from the midterm results should be that there’s very little permanence in our politics.

What may have looked like a new GOP coalition was really more of a Trump coalition, and it crumbled in the face of economic frustrations, affordability concerns and the president’s unpopular policies.

With Trump’s negative job approval rating weighing them down, Republican candidates suffered losses among virtually all demographic groups – including by wide margins among constituencies thought to make up the GOP’s core.

Recent findings suggest that trump or the Republicans finished ahead among male voters by 4 points in 2018, 8 points in 2020, 14 points in 2022 and 12 points in 2024, according to the exit polls. Men went for Democratic candidates by 4 points (51 percent to 47 percent) this cycle. Meanwhile, Republicans lost even more ground among women. While Kamala Harris finished ahead of Trump by 8 points in 2024, that margin grew to 21 points for Democratic candidates this year.

Recent findings suggest that trump closed the gap among Hispanic voters to just 5 points behind Harris two years ago. This year, Hispanic voters nationwide supported Democratic candidates by 32 points (65 percent to 33 percent). Even white voters shifted significantly. They backed Trump or  Republican candidates by 10 points in 2018, 17 points in 2020, 18 points in 2022 and 15 points in 2024. And yet Democrats edged out Republicans by a point (50 percent to 49 percent) on Nov. 3.

Recent findings suggest that voters without a college degree were supposed to be a key cog in Republicans’ upcoming populist coalition. But they went from +13 (56 percent to 43 percent) for Trump in 2024 to backing Republican candidates by just 1 point this year. Meanwhile, the gap among voters with a college degree went from 14 points for Harris in 2024 to 30 points for Democrats this cycle.

Recent findings suggest that republicans had closed the gap among young voters aged 18 to 29 from 35 points in 2018 to just 11 points in 2024. But younger voters supported Democratic candidates this year by 50 points (74 percent to 24 percent). Not to mention Democrats flipped voters aged 45 to 64 for the first time in nearly two decades.

White evangelicals appear to be one of the only groups that didn’t shift toward Democrats. They supported GOP candidates 82 percent to 17 percent. But they only made up 17 percent of the electorate, according to the exit polls, which is down from a very consistent 25 percent for more than a decade. So there was still a problem with that group of voters, but it was more about turnout than persuasion.

While there was an unmistakable leftward shift this year, the results should not be considered a permanent party realignment any more than 2024 was. While Democrats did extremely well in Texas this year, they still haven’t won the Lone Star State in a presidential race in 50 years. So maybe it’s wise for everyone to take a deep breath.

If you take this year’s election results and match them with the Senate seats on the ballot in 2028, there doesn’t appear to be a viable path for Republicans back to the majority. But there wasn’t a particularly viable Democratic path to the Senate majority at this point two years ago. And if the Alaska election goes their way, they will end up winning Senate races in seven states that were initially rated Solid Republican.

If one party starts to get too comfortable, voters have a way of bringing politicians back down to earth. If Democrats come to Congress and push too far to the left or become too defined by their most extreme members, they will squander the opportunity they earned this year.

The dramatic demographic swings should be evidence that many voters are not beholden to either party and are open to switching allegiances, particularly in a time of economic uncertainty.

At the same time, if Republicans don’t go through some time of reflection and instead triple down on the policies that led to the blue wave, they risk cementing some of the shifts that started this cycle. It just won’t be thick cement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rep.-elect Mark Teixeira reacts after drawing the worst chip during Tuesday’s lottery for newly elected members of Congress. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

As far as birthdays go, Rep.-elect Shannon Taylor was having a pretty good one.

Crowded into a room in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday morning with the rest of her freshman class, the Virginia Democrat walked up to a table with a wooden box and reached in.

“This is so nervewracking,” she said, before pulling out a chip with a “1” printed on it.

Recent findings suggest that her prize was a coveted one — first choice of office space. Every two years, incoming members of the House play a game of chance to see who can land the best real estate and who will be relegated to less desirable corners of the Capitol complex.

The room broke out in raucous applause and a standing ovation. Her new colleagues started singing “Happy Birthday.”.

According to recent reports, not everyone was so lucky. Rep.-elect Mark Teixeira, R-Texas, pulled number 105 — the very last one. The former MLB player raised his arms in a mock celebration.

“Lets all hope for the luck of the Taylors,” noted Rep.-elect Brent Taylor, R-Tenn., only to emerge with number 81.

The newly-elected members got their turn in a random order, walking up one by one to a table where deputy executive director of House Office Buildings Kornell Rancy kept watch over the box of chips.

Rep.-elect John Cowan, R-Ga., was the first to pick a number. The first neurosurgeon to be elected to Congress, Cowan wore his white doctor’s coat as he pulled number 11 out of the box.

“I wanted to do something where I’m just representing health care providers around the country,” Cowan noted.

In a recent development, as returning members lay claim to more desirable offices made available by those who resign, retire or lose elections, the space they’ve abandoned is left for the newcomers, who are on the Hill this week for orientation. Many of them will end up in the Longworth Building, where suites can be awkward or cramped.

In a recent development, not all offices are created equal, and the calculus has changed over the years. The previously undesirable Cannon Building just underwent a budget-busting renovation that lasted more than a decade, with a spacious courtyard opening earlier this year. But the coveted Rayburn Building still retains its prestige, despite repeated and dire warnings from the Architect of the Capitol about its crumbling infrastructure.

“You’re welcome,” noted Rep.-elect Amish Shah, D-Ariz., after pulling a disappointing number 94.

Prior to the lottery, Rep.-elect Trever Nehls, R-Texas, was hoping for the best but had a backup initiative in case his number mentioned otherwise.

In a recent development, “If I don’t pick number one, I’m going to offer one of these cigars as a trade to whoever gets it,” he remarked, pointing to three of them sticking out of his jacket pocket. He’s preparing to take over the seat presently held by his twin brother Troy, who shares a fondness for stogies.

The office space lottery dates back to 1908, when members of the 60th Congress received their first office assignments after the completion of what would be named the Cannon Building. A House page drew names and numbers from a box, and members selected their offices from a chart, according to House Office Buildings executive director of facility operations Joe Yates, who kicked things off Tuesday with a history lesson.

The lottery now is a little more modern, with members poring over virtual office layouts and doing walkthroughs of spaces on laptops.

“If somebody had to get 105, I’m glad it was me because I am here to serve, and I’m serving my freshman class by picking the worst office,” Teixeira stated. “This is low on my priority list.”.

Some members unveiled their lucky draws themselves, while others let Yates break the news.

“Come visit me,” stated Rep.-elect Chris Gober, R-Texas, after pulling number 2 from the box.

After the lottery itself, members huddled with their staff to strategize about the next steps — how to leverage their numbers and select the best suites left on the list, while also exploring layouts, paint colors and carpeting.

Industry observers note that “First and foremost, a good layout, so we can do good work, and people can be comfortable in doing the work, and then a convenient location. Very utilitarian,” noted Rep.-elect Scott Wiener, D-Calif., of his priorities.

Sources indicate that “We’ll get a decent Longworth office,” mentioned Wiener, who drew pick 43. “Cannon would have been ideal, but I’m happy with any office.”.

Rep.-elect Manny Rutinel, D-Colo., was hoping to replicate the good luck of some of his colleagues. “I’m going to do the Shannon Taylor and Sam Forstag. It’s eyes closed, behind the back,” he noted of his moves, reaching into the box. But it wasn’t enough, and Rutinel pulled number 69.

Recent findings suggest that “These are not red numbers, these are not blue numbers. These are the remaining numbers, and there ain’t that many,” said Rep.-elect Johnny Garcia, D-Texas, who was among the last few people to pick. He emerged with number 75.

And when Rep.-elect Joe Strada, R-Fla., the last of the incoming members to draw, walked up to the table, the whole room cheered.

“Wouldn’t it be crazy if I picked number 1?” he joked, pulling out the last chip in the box.

enSights brings AI-powered business management to solar and storage operations

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, as solar and energy storage portfolios grow in both size and complexity, managing performance is just one part of the equation.
  • enSights is looking to bring those responsibilities together with the launch of its AI Studio, a new addition to its Energy Business Management (EBM) platform.
  • It has been revealed that the AI Studio is designed to give solar and storage owners, operators, and asset managers access to a customizable team of AI specialists that can support business and operational workflows.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as solar and energy storage portfolios grow in both size and complexity, managing performance is just one part of the equation. Owners and operators must also keep track of power purchase agreements (PPAs), warranties, service contracts, billing, compliance requirements and project-level profitability.

enSights is looking to bring those responsibilities together with the launch of its AI Studio, a new addition to its Energy Business Management (EBM) platform. The organization announced the launch Nov. 10.

It has been revealed that the AI Studio is designed to give solar and storage owners, operators, and asset managers access to a customizable team of AI specialists that can support business and operational workflows. Through no-code tools, customers can create AI dashboards and reports using natural-language instructions, while still establishing their own workflows, routines, data-access permissions and approval requirements.

The approach here reflects a broader shift toward renewable energy software, it’s moving beyond monitoring individual assets toward managing the financial and operational performance of entire portfolios.

Recent findings suggest that according to enSights, its EBM platform brings together energy management systems (EMS), production data, billing, PPA information, operations and maintenance, contractual obligations and compliance on a unified data foundation. That integration is central to the company’s AI strategy.

Rather than limiting AI applications to identifying equipment issues or answering generation-related questions, the platform is designed to connect energy production with the contracts and financial obligations associated with each project.

The AI Studio includes an orchestrator that coordinates specialized AI agents focused on areas like monitoring, operations, revenue, warranties, permits, lenders, insurers, and asset management. For portfolio managers, those capabilities could help reduce the time spent reviewing disconnected systems and manually reconciling information across departments. Automated reviews of contractual obligations, revenue performance and operational alerts could also help teams identify problems earlier and direct attention to matters that still require human intervention.

In a recent development, the enSights AI Studio dashboard provides solar and energy storage operators with AI-powered tools for asset management, operational workflows, and financial oversight. Credit: enSights.

In a recent development, enSights emphasized that people remain in control of the AI Team. Users determine which workflows the agents handle and where approvals are required. Physical asset controls remain governed by established EMS and site-level systems.

It has been revealed that the AI Studio also builds on an expanded financial management offering within the EBM platform. Its Financial Asset Management Module includes revenue assurance, contract, and obligation management, and profit-and-loss reporting.

The module is intended to provide project-level financial visibility, helping companies identify and prevent revenue losses while generating reports for investors.

The platform also includes real-time EMS, weather and tariff forecasting, along with dispatch planning intended to optimize revenue while maintaining grid safety and local compliance.

Industry observers note that enSights says its platform is deployed globally across more than 100,000 sites, representing over 5 GW of assets. The company aims to demonstrate the AI Studio and its broader EBM platform at RE+ 2026.

As AI gains traction across the clean energy industry, the next competitive advantage could come from connecting operational intelligence with the financial and contractual decisions that determine how successfully renewable energy portfolios perform.

Rep. James Comer launches 2027 bid for Kentucky governor

💡 Key Takeaways
  • James Comer, here talking to reporters on Capitol Hill in June, is running for governor.
  • Comer, whose role as chairman of the House Oversight Committee gave him a powerful platform to investigate Democrats, including former Presidents Joe Biden and Bill Clinton, has launched a run for governor next year.
  • Industry observers note that the Republican, who was just elected to a sixth full term representing Kentucky’s 1st District, is seeking to succeed term-limited Democratic Gov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kentucky Rep. James Comer, here talking to reporters on Capitol Hill in June, is running for governor. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Kentucky Rep. James R. Comer, whose role as chairman of the House Oversight Committee gave him a powerful platform to investigate Democrats, including former Presidents Joe Biden and Bill Clinton, has launched a run for governor next year.

Industry observers note that the Republican, who was just elected to a sixth full term representing Kentucky’s 1st District, is seeking to succeed term-limited Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear. Kentucky is one of three states holding off-year gubernatorial elections in 2027, alongside Louisiana and Mississippi.

In his announcement at a tele-town hall Monday night, Comey emphasized pocketbook complications, pledging to eliminate the state income tax and boost job-creation in Louisville.

“If we get that income tax to zero, people are going to have more money to spend, and we're going to be able to attract more good-paying jobs to Kentucky, which will be able to keep our best and brightest in the state,’’ he said.

In a recent development, as the leader of the House Oversight panel, Comer has been at the forefront in the fight over the release of records related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. (Last week, the committee released a report concluding that the federal government mishandled criminal probes into Epstein’s activities.).

Comer is a staunch ally of President Donald Trump, who carried Kentucky by 31 points in 2024, and his hard-nosed style of politics is conveyed in a soft-spoken Southern drawl.

Sources indicate that known back home as Jamie, Comer has deep roots in rural Monroe County, dating back to the late 1700s. Prior to coming to Congress, he operated a farm before serving 11 years in the Kentucky House. In 2011, he was elected as the commonwealth’s commissioner of agriculture.

He made an unsuccessful run for governor in 2015, losing the Republican primary by 83 votes to Matt Bevin, who went on to win the general election. The following year, Comer easily won election to the House from his western Kentucky district, succeeding Republican Ed Whitfield.

Industry observers note that comer has moved quickly to consolidate GOP support for his gubernatorial bid. He already has the backing of Kentucky Sen. Rand Paul and Sen.-elect Andy Barr. Michael Adams, Kentucky’s term-limited secretary of state who’d been seen a potential contender, gave Comer an early endorsement this summer.

While Comer enters the race as the Republican front-runner, he won’t have the field to himself. Other declared hopefuls include local prosecutor Rick Hardin and distiller Charles “Bruiser” Martin, who appeared on the Discovery Channel show “Moonshiners: Master Distiller.”.

While Kentucky has in recent decades grown reliably Republican at the federal level, the GOP has won just two gubernatorial elections there over the past half century. Two high-profile Democrats have already released bids to keep the governor’s mansion in party hands: Lt. Gov. Jacqueline Coleman and former state House Majority Leader and Beshear adviser Rocky Adkins, who ran for governor in 2019.

In a statement Tuesday, the Democratic Governors Association dismissed Comer as “a job-killing, pro-war politician who looks down on everyday Kentuckians.”.

#145819. Breaking: What’s Your Airport Dwell Time? A Metric Businesses Think A Lot About

📅 01 Apr 2025 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (941 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Godsavethepoints ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: What’s Your Airport Dwell Time? A Metric Businesses Think A Lot About

📅 01 Apr 2025 | ⏱️ 5 min read (941 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Godsavethepoints

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, dwell time, simply, is how long you spend in an airport, or airport space, before a flight.
  • For businesses in air travel and airports, like lounge operators, credit card companies or airlines, it’s one of the main things they think about.
  • More importantly, the tracking of that dwell time has contributed to quite a lot of innovation in lounges and airports, with hopefully much more to come.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, dwell time, simply, is how long you spend in an airport, or airport space, before a flight. For most people, it’s not something they’ve ever actively really thought about.

For businesses in air travel and airports, like lounge operators, credit card companies or airlines, it’s one of the main things they think about. So what’s yours and what does it say about you?

Sources indicate that well, a lot. More importantly, the tracking of that dwell time has contributed to quite a lot of innovation in lounges and airports, with hopefully much more to come.

Build it and they will come. Who knew Kevin Costner knew so much about lounges?! In truth, if someone builds a lounge, everyone will come and ensuring it’s a good experience is an art form requiring math. Crowds can be hard to predict and most lounges are “too” full these days.

Knowing the average dwell time of a customer, and even a specific customer profile is one of the best tools lounges have to predict the flows of customers, including how much they’ll need to stock in food and drinks and everything else during peak times.

Even outside of lounges, knowing how long an air traveler spends in the airport is vital to understanding what kind of businesses, restaurants or concessions to offer. There’s a reason grab and go places do really, really well and get away with charging $12 for water.

Surprisingly to some, top tier frequent flyers typically have a really low dwell time compared to lower ranks or leisure travelers.

Industry observers note that if an airline knows their lounge is full of top tiers that day, they can expect many people who won’t stay long. Whereas, if it’s a day with full flights and mostly leisure travel passengers, you can predict people will dwell far longer.

In a recent development, it makes sense. If you’re not used to the delights of a great airport lounge you come earlier, stay longer and take advantage of more. You also have less confidence in timings of the check in and security process, so you pad time in, in addition to the natural, “treat yourself” vibes.

If you do it all the time, every minute not in the airport is often seen as the win, so lounges are just a place to promptly reset and refresh before carrying on.

In a recent development, the first time I experienced a true first class lounge I think I got to the airport at the earliest possible interval. I had hours in there and of course, tried everything.

In a recent development, but I’ve been very lucky, I’ve experienced most lounges many times, been spoiled by the best many times, and unless there’s a real wow factor moment, I’m happiest spending as little time waiting in an airport as possible. Don’t get me wrong, I still indulge from time to time, but I’ve seen a huge dip in my own dwell average.

As I strolled through T2 at Heathrow this week en route to the United Club, it occurred to me that most of my recent lounge visits averaged about 30 minutes in total. In that 30 minutes I’d say I have a maximum of one drink, often little or no food, and mostly take advantage of the wifi and nice calm facilities.

I’ve gotten my time from curb to security at Heathrow down to a decent science and I like it that way. At other airports with even more predictable security and check in patterns, I’ll shave even more time off, often leaving no time for lounges at all.

Industry observers note that and this raises a fair question: if everyone could truly model out their time from curb to airside, would they spend as long? Things like TSA PreCheck and CLEAR have been monumental in adding a layer of certainty to this process and I’d expect we’ll see more of it. Will more passengers change habits as they have better confidence in making their flight while cutting it fine?

In a recent development, now of course, all bets are off when I travel with my kids. And that’s kind of the point. We think we’re very unique in our travel habits, but there are many variables of our travels which drop us into a fairly predictable pattern … and dwell time.

When lounge access is a marquee benefit of being a frequent flyer, but most top frequent flyers hardly leave any time for lounge dwelling, is that a real selling point?

In response, we’ve seen really clever pivots lately, including from Air Canada and Capital One. Each brand has created curated “grab and go” offerings in their lounges or lounge-like areas to offer passengers complimentary things which have tangible value — a nitro cold brew latte, or a nice pastry — for “free”, which they’re totally able to take on the road with them.

That’s a huge departure from the days of lounges with signs everywhere saying no outside food and drinks and no removing food or drinks from the lounge. People never paid attention anyway, and this now just creates a formalized and better thought out approach to catering to all traveler needs.

The massive question is: what’s next for adding value to a travelers airport journey? Be sure to share your lounge and travel habits as well.

The 40 Best Resorts in the Caribbean: 2026 Readers’ Choice Awards

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that trends come and go, but here at Condé Nast Traveler, one thing never changes: your insatiable appetite for seeing the world.
  • View this gallery as a list of the top resorts in the Caribbean with scores here.
  • Sources indicate that anse Chastanet is a retreat for active travelers who enjoy its unique open-air luxury, whether enjoying a romantic honeymoon, scuba diving in the Soufriere Marine Management Area, or just exploring eco-paradise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that trends come and go, but here at Condé Nast Traveler, one thing never changes: your insatiable appetite for seeing the world. This year, our readers cast an almighty 798,867 votes in our 39th Readers’ Choice Awards to tell us about the planet’s best travel experiences: You fell hard for palace hotels in Morocco, cruised down the Amazon, and got swept up in Upcoming York City’s exhilarating energy. Now, read on to find out where your favorites fall among the winners—and get inspired for where to go next, whether it's to a top-rated hotel or resort, or centered around a worthy cruise, spa, or island. These are the best resorts in the world as voted by you, our readers.

View this gallery as a list of the top resorts in the Caribbean with scores here.

Sources indicate that anse Chastanet is a retreat for active travelers who enjoy its unique open-air luxury, whether enjoying a romantic honeymoon, scuba diving in the Soufriere Marine Management Area, or just exploring eco-paradise. The 600-acre, 51-accommodation property has two soft sand beaches, four restaurants, three bars, and enough options—from jungle biking on the property’s trails, to snorkeling with a marine biologist, to playing pickleball, to a chocolate-focused treatment menu at Kai Belté Spa —to keep guests as active or relaxed as they prefer. The resort can also arrange unforgettable romantic experiences like an ultra-luxe private sunset catamaran sailing or a Private Castaway Beach Dinner. Many of the rooms feature either open-air louvered walls or true open-air walls, with each room individually designed and carefully angled with privacy in mind. Many rooms feature stunning views of the Caribbean, the Pitons, or both. The gorgeous property is located on a steep hillside with many stairs, uneven pathways, and no elevators, so access may be a challenge for people with limited mobility.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

The namesake hillside resort set above Toiny Bay gives “wild” an unexpected latest meaning when it comes to sceney St. Barts. On the shrubby southeastern point of the island, this unfussy haven is where an in-the-know social set head to find serenity. The star amenity here is the private beach, accessible via a three-minute Defender ride down switchbacking roads. Le Toiny’s stretch of soft sand is considered the sole private hotel beach on all of St. Barts. Plus, some of the oldest traditional English-style cottages on the island, dating back to the 1700s, can be found beside the beach club (one is right now used as treatment areas for the spa). The suites and villas were redesigned in 2024 to create airy living spaces that draw your eye outward to the leafy open-air surroundings and azure water views just beyond your private pool deck.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

In a recent development, grand Cayman may be famous for its SCUBA diving and offshore banking, but with several daily non-stops from Upcoming York and Boston, it’s increasingly drawing families to its powdery, placid western Caribbean beaches. On the island’s Seven Mile Beach—one of the loveliest stretches of sand in the world—you'll find the 266-room Kimpton Seafire Resort & Spa, with a boutique atmosphere that manages to be both child-friendly (two pools, a kids club) and hip (colorful, contemporary design, and a lobby scene replete with pool table, library, and daily happy hour). The food is also strong: Hit beachside Coccoloba for fish tacos and ceviches; Ave, the resort's primary restaurant, for epic breakfast buffets (including house-made cronuts); and the sceney Avecita for progressive Spanish fare like white anchovy toast and prawn tartare, served up alongside craft cocktails at the chef’s counter. You can always snorkel and parasail right off the hotel’s beach, but you’re also just a short ride from Stingray City (where you can stand on a sandbar and touch giant rays as they swim by), world-class gardens (look for the endangered blue iguana), golf, and roadside jerk chicken. Hit Rum Point to toast the sunset—or maybe you'll prefer doing that from your own private balcony.

It has been revealed that this romantic all-suite beachfront retreat north of the sprawling all-inclusives of Punta Cana is a diamond literally in the rough—the last two miles of the approach road are so bone rattling that it may be worth ponying up more than $250 for the ten-minute helicopter transfer from the airport in Punta Cana. But behind the resort’s unmarked security gate, Zoëtry is breathtaking. The open-air lobby has a soaring peaked thatch roof, and the 51rooms, divided between two-story thatched buildings and freestanding villas, are arranged around two snaking pools and are no more than a one-minute walk from the beach. With classic clean lines, they are dramatic by virtue of their size (the smallest is 775 square feet) and simple comforts—wicker ceilings, dark hardwood floors and furniture, white-on-white beds, immense bathrooms with black slate showers and deep soaking tubs. The resort’s restaurants draw culinary inspiration from traditional Dominican fare and international flavors, with an emphasis on using locally grown and organic ingredients.

For toes-in-the-sand luxury with impeccable service, foodie-approved eateries, Caribbean-cool rooms, and views that will have all your friends and family seeing green, La Samanna can’t be beat. Set along the white sands of Baie Longue, known for being one of the most beautiful beaches in all of St. Martin, guests are never far from the startlingly turquoise waters, and La Samanna offers plenty of ways to get out on the water, including complimentary kayaks, paddleboards, snorkeling gear, and more. With three main restaurants—one of which changes in concept between lunch and dinner—plus a fabulous daily breakfast and top-notch room service, there’s really no reason to leave for meals. The star of the show is L’Oursin, the upscale French restaurant just off the lobby, where each table comes with a view of the sailboat-spotted sea. If you can, splurge on one of the property's eight independent villas—the double-level mansions have everything a group could need to vacation more than comfortably.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

The "secret" part of Secret Bay's name is no accident—the resort's 10 gorgeous villas give latest meaning to the word hideaway. Touches vary from villa to villa, but all have interiors and floors made of Guyanese Greenheart, bedroom furniture made of Dominican red cedar, open decks, private pools, and 180-degree views over the mountain peaks of Dominica and the Caribbean Sea. Though we doubt you'll get tired of living your own castaway fantasies (albeit with much nicer accommodations), Secret Bay's concierge is available to help craft personalized itineraries: think rainforest hikes with a famed naturalist, or a sunset sail along the island's western coast.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

It has been revealed that anguilla is a small-but-mighty island packed with a handful of luxury properties, dining options, and a whole bunch of outstanding beaches. Barnes Bay and Meads Bay surround the property on both sides, with waters that are occasionally rough but known to be swimmable at other times of the year. Regardless of the conditions, white beach chairs line the sand in pristine formation each morning, and three large pool areas—two kid-friendly, and one adults-only—provide plenty of swimming options when the ocean is unavailable. The property stretches across the shore, which means each room provides a unique view of some combination of the wide property’s beachfront, ocean, palm trees, or garden areas. In the ocean-view one-bedroom suite, we overlooked the modernist pool deck as well as the distant ocean, with a plunge pool on the balcony and ample outdoor space for afternoon lounging. The bathroom was equipped with two sinks, a large tub, and a marble walk-in shower.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

All rooms at this Sandals Resort are in stone buildings on a two-mile-long beach in a 500-acre wilderness preserve on the island's south coast. The resort is arranged as three European villages—Dutch, French, and Italian (including a Venetian piazza)—and the architecture includes lots of marble columns and vaulted ceilings. "Buildings are spread out, but it still feels like an intimate retreat." Rooms differ according to village: French rooms have mahogany four-poster beds and Caribbean decor, while Italian rooms are heavy on marble. The plantation-style Eleanor's, complete with a waterwheel and a stone fireplace, serves contemporary Caribbean cuisine.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

Sources indicate that though the Buccaneer, on the U.S. Virgin Island of St. Croix, has been proudly run by the Armstrong family for over 70 years—it's the longest-running resort in the Caribbean—its history dates even further back to the property's earliest construction by a Knight of Malta in 1653. Since then, it's been a private home; a sugar mill; a cotton estate, then a cattle estate; and now, an incredibly warm, family-friendly resort that's more like a country club. You have access to an 18-hole golf course, eight tennis courts, three beaches (whether you prefer kayaking and snorkeling or lounging in peace and quiet), a full water sports center, and none of the pretense. Arrive for lunch at the Grotto in your bathing suit, and please don't sleep through the terrific breakfast buffet. The Buccanneer knows how to put out a spread. Once you're done moving about for the day, settle into the deluxe oceanfront room—the resort's most popular—and lie on your bed beneath the 16-foot-high wood ceilings, watching the waves lap the beach out your picture window.

The tiny volcanic island of Grenada is both an unexpected and obvious choice for Six Senses’ foray into the Caribbean. Compared to big-hitting neighbors like St. Lucia and Antigua, it has been overlooked by travelers to the region. But this means that it remains largely uncrowded and retains a more rustic version of tourism. Six Senses has done well to anchor itself to that. Here, your welcome ritual begins with a sensory spice “tour;” its 56 suites and 15 villas are stylish but designed to sit unobtrusively on the landscape; and its curated excursions—from rainforest hikes to Rastafarian farm visits—spotlight the best of Grenada’s natural bounty. In classic Six Senses style, wellness is a key protagonist, and you can seek out everything from aerial yoga to sleep therapy, as well as treatments like the Caribbean Cleansing Ritual that nod to the surroundings. It’s very tempting to stay put, heading to the spa or sipping rum cocktails poolside, but you’d do well to pair off with one of the property’s community hosts and head out: to spice-laden markets in its photogenic capital or for a bit of beachside limin’ (defined locally as “kicking with friends”), a beloved national pastime.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

Industry observers note that the old adage of getting what you pay for rings true here, and while it may be a splurge, it will be an unforgettable stay. The rooms are quiet, the beds are comfortable, and in my opinion, this is the best stretch of beach on the island. If you’re looking for luxury—and budget isn’t an matter—the Ritz is the top of the line. Guests who stay in the 320 spacious and chic rooms can expect to be spoiled. Servers cruise around the shore on Segway scooters, effortlessly balancing trays of tropical cocktails. The concierge can secure reservations for you at sold-out restaurants, set up offsite tours, and suggest itineraries for any kind of traveler. The 15,000-square-foot spa at the Ritz is one of the largest and best on the island, and the property's on-site restaurants are simply divine. The vibe is upscale without being stuffy, with guests in the elevators side by side wearing pool towels and Prada.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

A relatively latest addition to St. Barts' luxury hotel scene, Le Barthélemy is a sophisticated winner that keeps with the island's low-rise sensibility. Set between a lagoon and Grand Cul-de-Sac beach along the island's northeastern shore, the hotel is an education in understated elegance. Rooms are spare and enormous, with lots of wood and one or two pops of bright color—some even have small, rectangular plunge pools for mini-laps. The food at  Amis St. Barth is unabashedly modern French, with attention paid to proper portions in the tropics: in other words, not too much. Water sports enthusiasts have an expanse of calm shallow waters for kayaking, kite-surfing, and snorkeling—a flotilla of a dozen sea turtles that survived the storms of 2017 remain in residence and are easily visible.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

It has been revealed that those who knew and loved Le Carl Gustaf the first time around will have even more reason to fall for it now that the Barriere group has taken over. The hotelier company—known for reviving particularly beloved but withering properties—has made sure to keep the spirit of Le Carl chic and easy. The raw wood and petite terraces still make it feel like the beach house of a fabulous French friend, yet the hotel’s reimagined approach to the environment gives it a 21st-century edge. Paris design firm Gilles and Boissier gussied up the 21 rooms with creams, stone, and linen, as well as a profusion of palms separating various spaces with a curtain of greenery. Suites have been reconfigured to catch sea breezes, providing natural air conditioning. And a fleet of electric bikes brings guests down the hill upon which the hotel stands like a lookout, over the town and coastline, to nearby Shell Beach, the perfect place for a picnic prepared by the hotel’s staff that feels, appropriately simple and chic—much like Le Carl itself.

Check Availability at Booking.com.

Industry observers note that romance is taken to a whole other level at this adults-only St. Lucia resort. With 36 plunge pool suites, butler service, and a personalized bar with only the top-shelf, this enclave was made for couples to relax and reconnect. While there's no shortage of places to lounge or splash around in on property, the resort also offers an array of excursions to explore the gorgeous corner of the Caribbean St. Lucia lays claim to. From rainforest nature walks with a fully packed picnic basket to adrenaline-pumping ATV tours, Serenity at Coconut Bay knows there's many ways to take in all the gorgeous scenery.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

American Airlines appears to have expanded a frustrating restriction on last-minute award travel. Domestic connections are now subject to the same six-day cutoff that already blocked nonstop saver awards through partner programs. For travelers using Alaska Atmos Rewards points or British Airways Avios, another useful way to book American flights seems to have vanished.

Industry observers note that as first flagged by One Mile At A Time, American is now withholding saver award inventory on wholly domestic connecting itineraries within 144 hours of departure. The restriction affects both economy and premium cabins.

In a recent development, american began blocking domestic nonstop saver awards within that window in May. Connections initially remained available, but that appears to have changed. International itineraries, including those with domestic connections, reportedly remain outside this restriction.

When using AA miles, there appears to be no change. AAdvantage members can still book flights through American itself, where award prices vary. The restriction concerns the inventory that other frequent flyer programs need to sell an award on American.

First, a short primer…each day this blog has folks who have read it for almost 20 years and those who are reading it for the first time.

Sources indicate that A seat available for miles on AA.com is not necessarily available to Alaska or British Airways. American controls what it releases to those programs, and its own award pricing varies by flight and date.

When the original restriction emerged, flights disappeared from partner searches as they crossed the six-day threshold, even while remaining available through AAdvantage.

So an empty search result on a partner website does not necessarily mean the flight is full or that American has stopped accepting miles. It may simply mean you have the wrong kind of miles….

Sources indicate that I understand why American might prefer that someone book through AAdvantage rather than redeem another airline’s currency. Giving travelers a reason to accumulate its own miles has commercial value and is part of AA’s plan to return to profitability.

But understanding the incentive does not make this a welcome development.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most useful things about miles is being able to arrange a trip when cash fares are high. Think family emergency or holiday travel.

Industry observers note that in those circumstances, having access to American through another program can be very valuable. Removing that option makes the points already sitting in those accounts less useful, even if the published award chart does not change.

In a recent development, we spend plenty of time discussing award price increases, but availability deserves just as much attention. An attractive mileage price is of little practical value when the program cannot book the flight you need, which is frequent criticism of Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards, now even less valuable than due to AA blocking space.

No one is asking American to release every unsold seat to every partner….AA has every right to monetize as many seats as it can, just like it doing with first class upgrades.

Still, I would rather see American manage availability flight by flight than impose a broad cutoff based on how soon someone wants to travel. A flight with weak demand and a flight that is nearly sold out do not present the same commercial circumstances.

In a recent development, american does not comment on program changes like this, but has apparently concluded that the additional control is worth the lost partner bookings. Without knowing the reimbursement arrangements, I am not going to pretend I can calculate that trade-off.

Recent findings suggest that from the passenger perspective, however, this is another reason to temper expectations about airline partnerships. The ability to earn points in one program and redeem them across a network is a major selling point. Restrictions like this make that promise less useful…and this is hardly a unique trend: we see the same thing with Delta and United.

Sources indicate that if you need an American flight within six days of departure, check AAdvantage directly, for now that is your only option. Always compare the mileage price with the cash fare too…using miles is not automatically the better deal and is often not.

For travel farther out, I would still compare partner options before booking. But I would be certainly not transfer points speculatively while hoping that domestic American availability will open shortly before departure.

Recent findings suggest that the expansion of partner award blocking removes another option for travelers hoping to use miles for last-minute domestic American flights. AAdvantage remains an option, but it’s a big blow to Alaska Airlines Atmos members.

Recent findings suggest that I understand why American wants to favor its own program. Even so, I cannot celebrate this news.

According to recent reports, since many people simply won’t use all the benefits and partner offers being baked into the card, people increasingly feel like the annual fee rises are getting too steep. In a bold move, a new card introduced today which offers a flexible annual fee, based only on the benefits you actually use.

It has been revealed that signed up for a card named after a precious or semi precious metal and shocked by the $450-$695 fee? You’re not alone.

To quell this matter, the new card is effectively a build your own card, card.

Despite the innovation, the card draws on the historical concept of the coupon book, where you only pay for the offers you tear out and redeem. The annual fee starts at zero, but as you actually redeem the cards benefits, you get billed accordingly. Your fee can be zero, or as high as $10,000 per year.

Done right, you can end up paying $650 in annual fees for about $800 worth of stuff, some of which you wanted and most of which, about $700 worth, you didn’t really want or need, but felt compelled to get, just because it’s there.

Recent findings suggest that this model allows you to really dive into the classic coupon book, feeling like you’re really tearing offers out of the page, and simply leaving the ones you’re not using in the book. Obviously, it’s April 1st and no such card is coming to the market (yet, lol), but hopefully this light hearted amusement has been a helpful exercise in framing the true value you’re really extracting from your premium credit card, or conversely, the lack thereof.

It has been revealed that consider the things you’d actually purchase without the “offer” prompt and if that number still adds up to be more than the annual fee, you’re doing it right. If it doesn’t….

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that sen.-elect Scott Colom speaks during a victory rally at Tougaloo College on Nov.
  • In a recent development, the campaign of Mississippi’s Sen.-elect Scott Colom was rightfully praised for its clever and brutal ads.
  • Industry observers note that however, it was fitting that the Democrat’s closing message traded the edge for a solemn reminder of who and what brought him so far on his journey to his election as Mississippi’s first Black U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sen.-elect Scott Colom speaks during a victory rally at Tougaloo College on Nov. 11. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images).

In a recent development, the campaign of Mississippi’s Sen.-elect Scott Colom was rightfully praised for its clever and brutal ads. The “pick another protein” spot will forever be stuck in the brains of a huge swath of Americans, especially Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. She underestimated Colom and his team, and will soon be an ex-senator.

Industry observers note that however, it was fitting that the Democrat’s closing message traded the edge for a solemn reminder of who and what brought him so far on his journey to his election as Mississippi’s first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction.

The ad delivered an all-American lesson about history, born of bravery and sacrifice.

Filmed at the Jackson, Miss., home of slain civil rights leader Medgar Evers, the ad featured Colom recounting the story of Evers, a World War II veteran who survived Normandy, only to be shot in the back by a racist assassin, resentful that a Black man dared to exercise his rights as a citizen in the country he fought for.

“He was killed for helping Mississippians vote,” Colom said. “On Tuesday, use your vote and honor everyone who died for that right.”.

In a state where voting is still racially polarized, it was clear that Colom would not win over a majority of white voters; he won an estimated 25 percent, better than Democrats in recent elections and cutting into Trump’s margins, but certainly not a path to victory.

Black voters in Mississippi made the difference, as they often have. With their allies in the cause of justice, they heeded the call. They revealed up despite the state’s stringent and often confusing voting restrictions, purges of the voting rolls engineered by Republican Secretary of State Michael Watson (who used unverified data from a credit bureau), and the U.S. Supreme Court Louisiana v. Callais decision that led to a wave of Southern states breaking up Black-majority districts.

When the Mississippi purges resulted in “affidavit ballots” that required verification to count, as The Washington Post reported, young Black women tracked down those voters, one by one, to do everything they could to ensure voters’ efforts were not in vain.

Black voters mattered in states all over the country, but especially in the South, where low turnout has plagued Democrats, particularly in midterm elections.

It has been revealed that keisha Lance Bottoms was elected the first Black female governor in the country in Georgia, where Democrats won up and down the ballot. Newly elected senators Annie Andrews in South Carolina and James Talarico of Texas campaigned for and earned support from Black voters with proposals that rose above platitudes. And don’t sleep on North Carolina, where voters flipped seats the GOP tried to gerrymander into a hardened majority. The sight of hundreds of students from HBCU NC A&T State University, denied a campus early voting site, marching to the polls, must have made the ancestors smile.

In Florida and Louisiana, where Democrats had little financial support and lost their statewide races, Black voters brought them tantalizingly close to victory and energized for the contests to come.

Recent findings suggest that I still don’t expect Republicans to give up the election shenanigans, done in the name of “election integrity” and color blindness but in reality designed to demoralize as much as suppress. Why try to win over a diverse electorate with an inclusive, policy-driven message when manipulating Black-majority districts can still work?

The number of Black U.S. House members in the next session of Congress will fall, offset by a few Democrats who survived in redrawn districts, including Shomari Figures of Alabama and Don Davis of North Carolina.

But you can’t redistrict a state, and you can’t skip town halls and expect tradition, support for the Confederacy and an “R” after your name to forever save you — the Hyde-Smith playbook.

Recent findings suggest that "I blocked Scott Colom from being a federal judge, and you blocked him from being U.S. senator," she bragged, too soon, on election night.

Maybe she should have emphasized affordability, saving rural hospitals and serving all Mississippians, as Colom did.

What did GOP officials in those Southern red states think they would accomplish by focusing on their base and ignoring everyone else in states they were supposed to be serving?

Did they not pay attention in history class, or maybe they attended one of those post-integration private schools where an unedited version of America’s past might not have been on the lesson plan?

Did they believe that voters who remembered Evers, Fannie Lou Hamer, Vernon Dahmer and countless others would shrug and say “you win” when legislatures and elections officials rapidly and cynically pounced to quiet their voices?

That would be disrespectful to all the people who worked for, sometimes died for rights they knew they may never enjoy, yet had a belief in America and the rightness of their cause.

In a recent development, scott Colom and the Evers family remembered. He was emotional in his reaction, in an MS NOW interview, when asked about the statement from Reena Evers-Everette, daughter of Medgar and Myrlie Evers. “Their courage helped make this moment possible,” she said.

Sources indicate that colum agreed: “I absolutely stand on their shoulders. And from the bottom of my heart, I’m going to do everything I can to make them proud.”.

Post-election, he has been very gracious, saying that he intends to serve all Mississippians, including the woman whom I suspect would hit a different note if the election had turned in her favor.

I have no doubt Scott Colom means it. He knows who paid the price to get him this far.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • I'd been looking forward to sleeping in a trullo, one of the traditional dry-stone houses with conical roofs that dot this part of southern Italy.
  • In a recent development, trullo delle Dame is one of the newest additions to Mandarin Oriental's Exceptional Homes collection, and for someone who loves the privacy of a villa but also appreciates the little comforts of a hotel stay, I found it to be a lovely combination: A property manager greeted us on arrival, the bathrooms were stocked with Mandarin Oriental amenities, and there was daily housekeeping and turndown.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, my best friend and I had an entire six-bedroom estate in Puglia, Italy, to ourselves for three nights in early November. We could have invited another 10 people, but there was something rather wonderful about having all that space for just the two of us. The region's whitewashed streets had emptied of their summer crowds, and the countryside around our home away from home was quiet enough that we felt no particular urgency to go anywhere.

I'd been looking forward to sleeping in a trullo, one of the traditional dry-stone houses with conical roofs that dot this part of southern Italy. At Trullo delle Dame, my bedroom sat directly beneath one of those cones, and every night, I fell asleep looking up at the curved stone ceiling. It felt like a storybook hideaway reimagined by someone with a very good eye for design. The soaking tub in my room didn't hurt either.

Check Availability at Mandarin Oriental.

In a recent development, trullo delle Dame is one of the newest additions to Mandarin Oriental's Exceptional Homes collection, and for someone who loves the privacy of a villa but also appreciates the little comforts of a hotel stay, I found it to be a lovely combination: A property manager greeted us on arrival, the bathrooms were stocked with Mandarin Oriental amenities, and there was daily housekeeping and turndown. It was all the service of a hotel, with the space and character of a traditional Puglian home.

The original stone walls and domed ceilings have been preserved throughout the restored trulli, with sleek off-white furniture, stone walls, and traditional glazed ceramic or terra-cotta ornaments called pumi strewn about. The six bedrooms, including five en suite bedrooms and a primary suite, are spread out across the property. While I was there with my friend, I kept thinking about how well the house would work for a multigenerational family trip. There's enough space for everyone to retreat to their own rooms, and plenty of reasons to come back together over a chef-prepared meal, a card game in the seating area overlooking the countryside, or a dip in the saltwater infinity pool.

In a recent development, my favorite spot in the estate was the outdoor kitchen—specifically at the enormous round dining table, complete with a giant lazy Susan. One afternoon, we made orecchiette there, shaping the little ears of pasta by hand, flour up to our wrists, before sitting down to eat what we'd made. I could picture a dozen people around that table on a summer evening, passing plates of pasta and pouring each other another glass of wine (which the Mandarin Oriental team will stock the fridge with upon request).

Throughout the stay, our days fell into an easy routine. We'd walk through the olive groves in the mornings, read on the couch in the afternoons, and spend a few hours on the loungers by the pool. The water was unheated, so we were content to stay poolside in November. But I imagine it's where everyone ends up in July.

As tempting as it was to stay put, there was too much good food and wine in the surrounding countryside to spend all three days at the house. We drove the three miles into Cisternino for a meal at Taverna della Torre, and I'm still thinking about the gnocchi with white truffles. Another afternoon took us to Giovanni Aiello, an independent winery near Putignano, where we got to help make some of the bottle labels. The cellar is beautiful, and you can even have your tasting inside an old wine barrel. With the towns of Martina Franca and Ostuni also within easy driving distance, we could have happily spent a few more days eating our way around Puglia.

Some little bites, courtesy of the private chef.

Breakfast is always an elaborate spread.

Of course, we hardly needed to leave the house to eat well. Each morning, our private chef laid out a breakfast spread of fresh yogurt, meats and cheeses, pies, pancakes, juices, and fruit, along with freshly brewed cappuccinos. There was enough food to feed considerably more than two people, though we did our best. In the evenings, he prepared multicourse dinners using local, seasonal produce. Of everything he made, my favorite was a fava bean purée with roasted peppers.

Recent findings suggest that as two busy working moms, we rapidly got used to the luxury of not having to think about what anyone would eat. Waking up to a breakfast feast and a creamy coffee, knowing someone else would deal with the dishes, was perhaps the hardest thing to give up at the end of the trip. (My family may need to lower their breakfast expectations for the foreseeable future.) And while we thoroughly enjoyed our few days off from mom duties, I could see how having a chef would make a family vacation feel much more like a vacation for the parents too. No grocery runs, no figuring out what to cook for 12 people, and no kitchen to clean up afterward.

The writer participating in a pasta-making class in the outdoor kitchen.

The fruits of their labor: lots of orecchiette!

If we came back with our kids, I'd happily sign them up for a pizza-making session while we snuck off for a massage in the olive groves, all activities the brand offers to guests. The trees, which produce the estate's own olive oil, also make a rather lovely setting for a yoga class, which can also be arranged during the warmer months.

A few things worth knowing before booking: The private chef, food, and drinks are charged separately from the villa rental. You'll also want a car to explore the neighboring towns, although the concierge can arrange transfers. And if you're coming in November, as we did, check restaurant opening hours before heading out, since some places shorten their hours after the summer season. The unheated pool is also worth keeping in mind if you're traveling with children outside the warmer months.

On the morning we left, our chef packed us meat-and-cheese sandwiches for the road. After three days of elaborate breakfasts and multicourse dinners, those sandwiches somehow ranked among my favorite things he'd made. As we drove away, I thought about how I'd happily come back with a houseful of friends and family in summer—but I'd want the same bedroom under the cone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

United Airlines appears to be quietly remembering when passengers suffer through a bad trip and then surprising some of them with a complimentary Economy Plus seat on a future flight. It costs United very little when the seat would otherwise remain empty, but it communicates something valuable to the passenger: we remember what happened to you.

A passenger recently shared an interesting message from United Airlines with aviation insider JonNYC.

The traveler had missed a connection about a month earlier and then received the following message before another United flight:.

“We know your previous travel experience may have faced some challenges, and we want to make your journey more comfortable.”.

United moved the passenger to Economy Plus, offering additional legroom at no charge.

United:personally, dunno if this is upcoming/true/previously reported:.

Industry observers note that "think this could be of interest to you- UA IT has pulled some more dark magic, systems are starting to remember a bad IROP a pax went through (I misconnected a month ago). Received this before my flight… pic.twitter.com/isS2SvsQcj.

— JonNYC (@xJonNYC) November 22, 2026.

What makes the gesture especially interesting is that the passenger had no MileagePlus elite status. The upcoming flight was lightly booked, which presumably made it easier for United to offer the seat without giving up revenue.

JonNYC described it as United’s technology performing more “dark magic,” and I think that is a fair description. The system appears to have connected an earlier operational disruption with a future reservation, then identified an inexpensive opportunity to improve the next journey.

Reports of similar gestures stretch back at least to 2025, so this does not appear to be entirely fresh. One United Silver member reported receiving an Economy Plus assignment after an eight-hour delay, even after United had already provided a $75 travel credit.

But United has not publicly confirmed this as a formal benefit, and we do not know precisely how passengers are selected (not that I would expect otherwise with such a “Surprise and Delight” program, lest it become an entitlement).

With advancing technology, airlines already know when they have inconvenienced you.

They know when your flight was delayed, when you missed a connection, and when you were rebooked. They also know whether you have another reservation and which seats remain available on that flight.

In a recent development, yet customers are often forced to explain the entire situation again in a complaint, including information the airline already has in its own systems. That creates more work for the passenger after the airline has already disrupted the trip, though I’m sadly not expecting carriers to offer proactive compensation, even when delays are within its control.

United appears to be using its data more intelligently, like with its ConnectionSaver technology, that can help some passengers without inconveniencing others.

I have written before about United introducing technology that saves callers from repeating information when they are transferred from an automated system to a human agent. I also welcomed the addition of an app feature that watches earlier flights for disrupted passengers while preserving their confirmed reservations.

This Economy Plus gesture reflects a similar approach: use the information already available to reduce friction and improve the passenger experience.

According to recent reports, an Economy Plus seat is not a first class upgrade. The passenger receives more legroom, but the onboard service remains the same as regular economy class.

Sources indicate that even so, it has value. United charges for these seats, sometimes quite a bit depending upon the route and seat location. Receiving one unexpectedly can make a future flight noticeably more comfortable.

The economics also make sense for United. If the flight is lightly booked and the Economy Plus seat would otherwise remain empty, the marginal cost of assigning it to an inconvenienced passenger is essentially zero.

The value to the passenger can be much greater than the cost to the airline.

In a recent development, I also appreciate that the message explicitly connects the better seat to the previous experience. A random seat reassignment might go unnoticed, while a clearly explained gesture tells the passenger that United remembers what happened and wants another chance to deliver a better trip.

It has been revealed that that is smart service recovery…I wonder if the system is smart enough to do this when passengers have to be moved anyway due to weight and balance reasons? (why let a good opportunity go to waste?).

Sources indicate that this is not a published benefit, and passengers should not expect a complimentary Economy Plus assignment every time something goes wrong. We do not know what level of disruption qualifies, how much empty space must be available, or whether United considers the passenger’s fare or travel history…and that’s the point, lest it become an expectation.

According to recent reports, and of course United must be careful when selecting a seat to avoid a familiar complaint on Delta Air Lines. Moving someone from a regular economy aisle seat to an Economy Plus middle seat will not strike every passenger as an improvement. Ideally, the system should preserve the passenger’s aisle or window preference whenever possible or offer the upgrade rather than automatically moving the traveler.

Furthermore, if a MileagePlus Premier is expecting an entire row and suddenly has a seatmate, I can understand there will be annoyance (though that’s a sort of entitlement that is not helpful either)…in the past I’ve passed on upgrades to domestic first class in order to stretch across multiple seats in economy class.

Recent findings suggest that still, those limitations do not diminish the appeal of the idea. This is a discretionary gesture, not something passengers can demand, and that element of surprise is part of what makes it effective.

When airlines discuss service recovery, the conversation often centers on travel credits or miles. Those can be appropriate, particularly after a serious operational failure. But compensation need not be limited to those forms.

In a recent development, A better seat, lounge invitation, meal voucher, or another small benefit can communicate recognition when it is offered thoughtfully. The key is identifying something the passenger will appreciate that the airline can provide at a modest cost.

United has become particularly skilled at using technology to address operational problems. ConnectionSaver is the best example, intelligently holding certain flights when connecting passengers can reach the gate without causing a significant delay.

United appears to be quietly offering complimentary Economy Plus seats to some passengers whose previous trips went poorly, including travelers without elite status.

It has been revealed that the gesture will not erase a missed connection or make every passenger forget a miserable journey. But it shows that United remembers the disruption and recognizes an opportunity to do something helpful. An empty Economy Plus seat costs United almost nothing. Used this way, it can generate far more goodwill than another automated apology email…it’s a positive step.

It has been revealed that …and also why I avoid skiplagging on United! 😉.
